system_description.narrative_title: Escalating Iran-led regional war, proxy strikes and diplomatic brinkmanship
system_description.narrative_summary: A cycle of military escalation—centered on Iran, its proxies (notably the Houthis), and a U.S.-led response—is colliding with intense diplomatic maneuvering (including Iran's repeated seven-day ceasefire proposals and renewed U.S.-Iran talks), allied realignments, and domestic U.S. political battles over war powers. As an open system, kinetic actions, bargaining signals, alliance decisions, and market responses continuously exchange information and resources with adjacent systems, producing reinforcing and dampening feedbacks that shape the trajectory toward either de-escalation or wider regional war.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: concrete actors (Iran, the U.S., Saudi Arabia and Gulf allies, the Houthis, Yemen, China, the U.S. Congress, international institutions), processes and states (military escalation and proxy strikes, ceasefire offers and direct talks, alliance signalling and diplomatic isolation, war-powers politics, control of energy chokepoints), and economic feedbacks (oil-price movements, capital flows, sanctions and alternative financial arrangements).
system_description.super_system: International security and global energy-economy system
adjacent_subsystems: U.S. domestic politics and law (war-powers, midterms, executive-congressional tensions)
Global oil markets, shipping and Strait of Hormuz security
China's strategic-economic networks (trade, financing, arms/kit transfers, currency platforms)
Regional conflict theatres (Yemen/Houthi front, Gulf states' internal security, Israel-related tensions)
evidence_headlines: Iran's president blames U.S., Israel for global instability in defiant UN speech
Houthis say they attacked Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu
US Senate rejects resolution curbing Trump's Iran war powers
Iran offers US new ‘7-day’ ceasefire proposal
US proposes $10bn fund with Arab allies to bypass Hormuz
Saudi Arabia quits China-led cross-border currency platform

variables.name: Military escalation intensity
variables.description: Overall intensity of kinetic military operations and direct armed engagements across the region.

variables.name: Proxy attack frequency
variables.description: Rate at which armed proxy forces carry out strikes or offensive actions per unit time.

variables.name: Ceasefire commitment strength
variables.description: Credibility and expected durability of ceasefire offers, commitments and pauses in hostilities.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement level
variables.description: Intensity and continuity of direct diplomatic talks, negotiations and mediation activity among adversaries and intermediaries.

variables.name: Alliance cohesion
variables.description: Degree of coordination, policy alignment and mutual support among aligned actors and partners.

variables.name: Executive warpower constraint
variables.description: Strength of domestic legal, institutional and political limits on executive use of military force.

variables.name: Energy transit disruption
variables.description: Extent to which energy transit routes and chokepoints are disrupted, threatened, or operationally constrained.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: Magnitude of short-term fluctuations in global hydrocarbon prices driven by conflict-related risk perceptions and supply threats.

variables.name: Capital flow sensitivity
variables.description: Responsiveness of cross-border capital movements, borrowing costs and investor withdrawals to changes in conflict risk.

variables.name: Sanctions pressure intensity
variables.description: Rate and severity at which economic sanctions, financial restrictions and asset freezes are applied or tightened.

variables.name: Alternative financial integration
variables.description: Degree to which actors adopt non-traditional financial channels, de‑risking measures and de‑dollarized payment arrangements.

variables.name: Public support for military action
variables.description: Aggregate level of public and political appetite for offensive military operations among relevant constituencies.

variables.name: Deterrence signaling intensity
variables.description: Frequency and escalation of overt threat communication, demonstrations of force, and coercive signaling between adversaries.

variables.name: Proxy logistics resilience
variables.description: Capacity of proxy networks to sustain supply lines, weapons deliveries and operational tempo under disruption.

variables.name: Diplomatic isolation level
variables.description: Degree to which actors experience withdrawal of diplomatic engagement, partnerships or multilateral access.

variables.name: Perceived escalation threshold
variables.description: Average perceived limit at which continued hostilities are believed to trigger broader regional war or systemic breakdown.

catalysts.title: Decision on Iran's 7-day ceasefire offer
catalysts.description: U.S./allies either accept, conditionally accept, or reject Iran's 7-day ceasefire proposal; outcome will change pause durability and talks momentum.
catalysts.rationale: Iran offers new seven-day ceasefire; Araqchi says now up to US; Trump reportedly rejects—decision imminent. (Headlines: Iran offers 7-day; Araqchi; Trump rejects.)

catalysts.title: Risk of renewed US bombing after midterms
catalysts.description: U.S. administration statements signal possible resumed large-scale strikes after U.S. midterm elections, shifting operational tempo and signaling.
catalysts.rationale: Exclusive: Trump rejects Iran ceasefire, expects renewed bombing after midterms. (Headline: Exclusive | Trump Rejects Iran Ceasefire... )

catalysts.title: Pre-election war powers vote in Congress
catalysts.description: Planned Congressional votes to curb or affirm executive war authorities before U.S. elections could change legal constraints on military action.
catalysts.rationale: Democrats tee up pre-election war powers vote; Senate recently rejected a curbing resolution. (Headlines: US Democrats tee up...; Senate rejects...)

catalysts.title: Continued Houthi strike campaign
catalysts.description: Ongoing Houthi missile/drone strikes on Saudi ports, oil facilities and shipping lanes likely to persist, threatening energy transit and prompting allied responses.
catalysts.rationale: Houthis claim strikes on Riyadh, Aramco; allies unite behind Saudi; Houthi attacks on Yanbu and shipping reported. (Multiple headlines)

catalysts.title: Creation of $10bn fund to bypass Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: U.S. proposal to set up a $10bn fund with Arab allies to create alternative energy transit routes and infrastructure to reduce Hormuz vulnerability.
catalysts.rationale: US proposes $10bn fund with Arab allies to bypass Hormuz; intended to reduce transit vulnerability and boost coordination. (Headline: US proposes $10bn fund...)

catalysts.title: Continuation of U.S.–Iran high-level talks
catalysts.description: Ongoing direct talks between U.S. and Iran, with external backchanneling (e.g., Xi-Trump engagement), could alter escalation perceptions and pause durability.
catalysts.rationale: US and Iran hold first talks since June; Trump and Xi discuss Middle East war as Iran presses 7-day plan. (Headlines: US and Iran hold talks; Trump, Xi discuss.)

catalysts.title: Saudi exit from China-led currency platform (trend)
catalysts.description: Saudi withdrawal from a China-led cross-border currency platform signals a possible ongoing Gulf shift away from Chinese financial channels toward allied coordination.
catalysts.rationale: Saudi Arabia quits China-led cross-border currency platform; signals financial realignment and closer ties with allied partners. (Headline: Saudi Arabia quits China-led platform.)
